before:
MIMI: I've got a plan. Three clear steps, one shared folder... and a phone I appear to have filed somewhere exceptionally secure.
LULI: Please tell me the plan isn't on the phone. I've brought an emergency book, but it doesn't cover this.
DILO: I can help make it beep. If it's in your hand again, though, I'm counting that as my quickest solve.
after:
MIMI: All right. Files ready, team ready... where's my phone?
LULI: You said, 'Nobody move anything.' We took you seriously.
DILO: Do we get detective badges for finding it, or is that still a household chore?

before:
DILO: I can fit all my theories on that wall. I may have to write small around the really important ones.
LULI: And the evidence? Or is that going to have to book an appointment?
ALIO: We could put in a small shelf. Then the theories would look established, even the ones we made up five minutes ago.
NINI: For the theories? Mine needs a cushion. It's been standing around waiting for a fact.
BIBI: A question mark would be more useful. Then I can tell which ideas still need checking when I come back with the next file.
MIMI: No cushions on the Case Wall. Detective, bring your notes over here. This family has plenty of imagination; let's leave some room for what we can actually prove.
after:
DILO: I was thinking my best theories could go across the top. In big letters.
LULI: How big are the facts allowed to be?
ALIO: Mine can go underneath Dilo's. Then mine will look more reasonable.
NINI: Could I have that little corner? I want to write 'We don't know yet.'
BIBI: Leave her plenty of room. That's usually our biggest category.
MIMI: Everyone step back a little. I'd like our new detective to see the wall before we fill it with ourselves.

before:
MIMI: Internal stock. No courier. Good. We can check who was at Delivery without inventing anyone new.
ALIO: Or we investigate my leading theory: a secret tunnel and a minivan. Very efficient. Very suspicious. I haven't decided who drives.
LULI: A tunnel, a minivan, and zero evidence. Impressive start, Alio.
NINI: Let's park the minivan for a minute and follow the facts first. Detective, there's room for your notes here.
DILO: Good. It was blocking mine. If a tunnel turns up later, we'll apologize to the minivan. Until then, it stays in the margin.
after:
MIMI: The envelope came from inside the Academy. No courier. That gives us somewhere to start.
ALIO: I've already got a secret tunnel and a minivan. We could start there.
LULI: You've arranged transport before finding a single clue?
NINI: He drew the minivan first. It's got all our names on the seats.
DILO: Then I want a window. I can watch for the evidence on the way.

before: The Cup has returned itself with suspiciously good posture. Look at it. You'd think it had never left.
after: Look how neatly the Cup's sitting there. That is exactly how I put things back when I hope nobody asks where they've been.

before: It was signed out, Alio. That's allowed. Being polished afterwards is rather grand, but still not a crime.
after: We know. You line your shoes up after you've used someone's good scissors.

before: Then I withdraw my complaint about the Cup. Its paperwork, however, is doing an excellent impression of a blank page.
after: That happened once. And this Cup is much tidier than my shoes.

before: Better. We need someone who can help explain the missing handoff, not a confession from a trophy. I'll put the return sheet beside your map.
after: Well, I'm glad we've cleared the scissors up. The Cup still has a blank return sheet.

before: That may be Alio's fastest promotion from theory to useful question. You take the map, Detective. I'll watch the extremely well-behaved Cup.
after: I want to hear the scissors story later. The long version.

before: The trophy shelf is trying very hard to look important. I've appointed its brightest sparkle Inspector Glitter.
after: I've found a sparkle on the trophy shelf. I'm calling it Inspector Glitter.

before: Has Inspector Glitter found a difference between the photographs, or has it mainly been admiring its own reflection?
after: Has Inspector Glitter found any of our ten differences?

before: Mostly admiring. A difficult first case. I'll compare the pictures while it recovers from not being in charge.
after: Not yet. It likes that shelf too much to look anywhere else.

before: Should I be worried about my job? I can stand by a shelf looking important. I've practiced.
after: I could do that job. Stand somewhere shiny and look important.

before: Only if you start shedding glitter. Pass me Photo B, please. Let's give the whole room a proper look before the shelf gets any more attention.
after: You'd want a chair by lunchtime. Pass me the other photo.

before: That is a very suspicious black box. It's arrived at the wrong tent without looking remotely sorry.
after: I'll watch the evidence box. Alio, you can patrol the tents.

before: It's a labeled evidence box. The seal is intact. Let's save the interrogation voice for somebody who can answer.
after: That's generous. You get to sit down while he does all the walking.

before: Exactly. Suspicion with paperwork. You have to admire the preparation.
after: Someone has to stay with the box. I'm prepared to make that sacrifice.

before: Please don't interrogate the box before the people. Who was with Pixel? That's someone we can actually ask.
after: I'll find out who was with Pixel. They might actually have something to tell us.

before: May I stare at the box professionally while we find out? I think it's avoiding eye contact.
after: Can I make my report sitting down, or is that a senior detective skill?

before: You've been doing that for a full minute. If it blinks first, it can wear your helmet.
after: Sit beside your brother. I'll patrol. Apparently it takes two of you to stop a sealed box going anywhere.

before: I challenge you to beat my locker. I've given it a very stern talk about not embarrassing me.
after: Six symbols. One locker. Detective, shall we see which of us gets it first?

before: Does it know this is a competition? Or have you challenged a door without telling the door?
after: If the Detective solves it, are you going to say you were just about to?

before: It has been briefed. Begin when you're ready, Detective. The locker and I have cleared our afternoon.
after: Only if I was. Which I might be. It's important to keep that possibility open.

before: Then we shall read its clues politely. I'd hate to frighten it into forgetting its own code.
after: I'll leave a little space beside the answer for 'Dilo was nearly there.'

before: If the locker wins, does it get a badge? We'd need somewhere to clip it.
after: What if the locker beats both of you? Does it get a badge?

before: Absolutely not. Conflict of interest.
after: No. It already knows the answer. That's a very unfair advantage.

before: Four marks. One incomplete route. Does this printer ever send anything straightforward? 'Dear Dilo, here is the answer' would be a refreshing change.
after: Four matching marks, and still no explanation. Could the printer send a nice ordinary answer for once?

before: You'd complain there was nothing to solve. Then you'd check the back in case it had hidden the interesting bit.
after: You'd turn it over to look for the puzzle on the back.

before: Could it at least send something with a name? I've got 'the thing', 'the other thing' and 'the thing we mustn't lose'. My notes are becoming very unhelpful.
after: I'd settle for a name. My notes say 'the thing from the thing.' I knew what I meant when I wrote it.

before: I'll take these to the archive. Names, dates and something to compare them with. If the printer asks for me, tell it I'm checking its references.
after: Bring them to the archive with me. We can look for proper names while Dilo checks the backs of things.

before: I had emotionally prepared for a dragon tooth. There was going to be a drawing. Possibly a very impressive warning sign.
after: I'd already drawn the dragon. Now I've got a perfectly good dragon and a case about a spoon.

before: So had I. None of my plans involved stirring soup with a Roman spoon.
after: You could give it some soup.

before: Perhaps the dragon was a cook. We haven't checked its qualifications.
after: That works. It can be a dragon who cooks.

before: That explains the spoon. My history book's missing the chapter about Roman dragon chefs, though.
after: I'm interested again. Does it breathe fire into the pan, or is that why it needs the spoon?

before: We have a label and an object that disagree. Let's ask about that before we rewrite history.
after: I was trying to help Nini finish a drawing. I seem to have started a cookbook.

before: A relief. I've only just put history back on its shelves.
after: Leave me a page. I've burned enough dinners to contribute.

before: Can we keep the dragon in the margin? Pencil only. I know you're going to ask.
after: Grandma! You're supposed to be helping with the real history.

before: Good. Leave me room to object. You take the room record, Detective; we'll keep the imaginary dragon out of your way.
after: I am. Those dinners happened.

before: Alio, how many cupboards have you checked? Please tell me we're counting cupboards, not dramatic entrances.
after: Alio, was that the third cupboard or the fourth? I'm starting to recognize the brooms.

before: Only the dramatic ones. I opened the last one very slowly in case the moon was hiding behind the coats.
after: Fourth. I checked behind the coats as well.

before: The moon costume is larger than most cupboards. If it were behind the coats, the coats would be standing in the corridor.
after: That moon costume wouldn't fit behind the coats. It barely fits through a door.

before: Excellent. We've eliminated the little cupboards. I knew all that slow opening would produce results.
after: Then we've ruled out four cupboards. And all those coats.

before: A triumph of fieldwork. Let's check the room record next. The brooms and I are running out of conversation.
after: Splendid. Let's leave before I start calling the brooms by name.

before: My route is beautifully straight. No unnecessary turns, no wasted walking. Very impressive on paper.
after: My shortest route gets us there in almost no time. I even drew it in one stroke.

before: Have you shown it to the walls? They seem to have plans of their own.
after: Does that include the time we spend standing at locked doors?

before: The building has rejected my first draft. I was going to discuss it with the wall, but it hasn't offered an appointment.
after: Small delay while we reconsider.

before: Read the door signs first. You may find the building is easier to work with when you use its doors.
after: Would you like to reconsider here, or after we've all followed you there?

before: I'll hold the map. Please don't negotiate with any load-bearing walls. I'm not holding up the roof while you explain your route.
after: Here, please. I know his reconsidering face. I'd rather see it sitting down.

before: You're looking at that symbol as if it owes you an explanation. Do you know it?
after: You stopped halfway through saying something. Do you know that mark?

before: I remember something. That's not the same as knowing. Give me the record beside it before I start trusting a memory on its own.
after: I remember something about it. I want to check before I let you all run off with my memory.

before: I'll find it. We can check them together. You can keep the dramatic pause while I look.
after: I'll get the records. You can guard Alio while I'm gone.

before: While we're checking memories, I remember being promised cake on an investigation. Very clearly. Excellent detail.
after: While we're checking memories, I distinctly remember being promised cake on this investigation.

before: You promised yourself the cake, Alio. I was there for that announcement.
after: You promised yourself cake. Quite loudly. Nobody had a chance to agree.

before: A very reliable source. Terrible at delivery. I'd like to interview whoever was supposed to bake it. Unfortunately, I believe that's also me.
after: I was hoping one of you had agreed quietly. Now I'll have to bake it myself.

before: Two teams. One rover. One truly upsetting cable tangle. Nobody move; I can make this considerably more complicated.
after: Two teams claiming one rover. I could keep it here while we sort this out.

before: Which problem are you solving first? The rover, the cable, or your urge to take something apart?
after: Here beside you? How convenient.

before: The access record. We need someone who can help explain it. You may note that I said this before touching a screwdriver.
after: I know how to look after a rover. I could even fix that cable.

before: Correct answer. Disturbing speed. I'll untangle the cable while you recover from being sensible.
after: Dilo, you haven't looked at either ownership sheet. You've already found room for it next to your chair.

before: Careful. It may have a third owner. And please log that sensible moment separately; I may need it in a future family discussion.
after: Fine. Sheets first. But if anyone needs a temporary rover sitter, I'm still available.

before: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar. I think they were getting quite close.
after: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar.

before: It was undercover. You can't expect a good investigation to happen in the most obvious compartment.
after: It was undercover.

before: Does the oat bar know? It's been very quiet about its new colleague.
after: Does the oat bar know?

before: We protect our sources. And occasionally forget which compartment they're in. This is a complicated profession.
after: We protect our sources.

before: I'd like that entered in the bag report. Preferably next to the bit where you tell us to label everything.
after: Can I put that in the bag report? Right beside 'Always know where your equipment is.'

before: You would not.
after: You would not. Pass me my source. I haven't had breakfast.

before: Please speak clearly for the notebook. Name, reason for being here, and anything you remember about the password.
after: For the record: where did you hear those four words?

before: Try listening before your next question. It says 'cracker'. I don't think it's finished answering that one.
after: It's asking for a cracker, Dilo.

before: I've got 'cracker'. It keeps repeating it. At least its statement is consistent.
after: I heard. I've written it down three times. I was hoping we'd get to the password.

before: I think it's set a price. You're trying to run a serious interview and it's trying to order lunch.
after: It thinks you're taking its order.

before: I'll ask the handler. My first interview with a snack budget. Please don't tell Alio; he'll start charging biscuits for his theories.
after: Right. I'll ask the handler. First witness who's made me feel like a slow waiter.

before: My fox theory has one weakness. I'm prepared to hear it, as long as everyone remembers how good the rest of it is.
after: My fox theory has one weakness. I'm trying to work around it.

before: Pockets? Where was your fox planning to keep the camera?
after: Pockets?

before: Several weaknesses. I'm making a list. I had rather hoped the pockets would count as an equipment problem.
after: Exactly. Where does a fox keep a camera?

before: Add 'fox operating camera equipment'. And 'somebody teaching it'. This is becoming quite a large project for one fox.
after: It needs a little strap. Here, I'll draw one around its neck.

before: Cruel. Fair. I'll draw it a tiny camera strap, then let it retire from the case with some dignity.
after: Thank you. Someone has finally taken the equipment problem seriously.

before: Keep the drawing. Hand me the actual photo. The evidence is still stubbornly unfoxy, and I'd like to finish before you design its uniform.
after: Lovely. Now I want to see the fox. This is why I shouldn't sit next to you two.

before: One of these statements has broken the clock. I'd like the clock to know I was on its side.
after: Somebody sounds very sure about a journey that doesn't seem to fit.

before: Or somebody mixed up two moments. Before we arrest the clock, can we check that?
after: Maybe they've mixed up two moments. I've done that.

before: Could happen. I once announced I'd packed lunch. I'd packed three books. I'd been very thorough about the wrong thing.
after: So have I. I was absolutely certain I'd packed lunch once. Three books. Not a sandwich in sight.

before: I remember. Your bag was very well fed. You had to share my lunch, and the books didn't contribute a thing.
after: I remember. You kept checking the bag, as if lunch might be in a different chapter.

before: Three books? Not even one recipe? I'd have expected better preparation from this family.
after: Three books? Surely one of them had something to eat in it.

before: Not one on cooking. Next time you can check my lunch before we leave. You've become very thorough since the cake investigation.
after: A magnificent feast. I read it while Mom gave me half her sandwich.

before: Next trip: readable name tags. Big letters. Nothing that requires a family meeting to identify.
after: Next trip, big readable name tags. On every backpack.

before: I was going to suggest satellite tracking. A small dot on a screen for each bag. Possibly a theme tune.
after: I was going to suggest satellite tracking. We could find a bag anywhere on Earth.

before: My tags work indoors, don't need charging and won't announce our arrival every time we walk into a room.
after: With a tag, I can find mine without asking you to charge anything.

before: Ruthless. You've beaten me with a piece of cardboard. May I at least draw a satellite on mine? I'd like to lose with dignity.
after: Fine. One for each bag. And a little one for your phone, since we're solving family problems.

before: That hat could shelter the whole team. If it rains on our next investigation, I know where I'm standing.
after: If it rains on our next case, I'm standing under that hat.

before: It also had an excellent detective underneath it. I brought the hat for company, not for a review of its roof space.
after: Ask first. There may be a grandmother under it.

before: We're finding the photograph's date, not the hat's. Admire it all you like; it doesn't tell us when the picture was taken.
after: She used to make me carry it in a separate bag. My sandwiches traveled underneath.

before: Finally, a sensible Academy policy. My wardrobe has suffered quite enough questioning for one afternoon.
after: And arrived in perfect condition. You're welcome.

before: Can we still admire it respectfully? I think Alio wants to add an extra room.
after: So Alio's not wrong. We could all fit under there.

before: Within controlled limits. One more room and I'm charging rent. Now pass me the photograph, please.
after: You may visit. No one is moving in.

before: Railway-investigation helmet: deployed. Ready for tracks, tunnels and announcements that sound unnecessarily urgent.
after: Helmet on. Ready for the railway investigation.

before: It's the same helmet. You wore it to the last investigation.
after: We're in the ticket hall. The biggest danger so far is you turning around with that backpack.

before: It has changed departments. Please respect its professional development.
after: I've been giving you plenty of warning.

before: Then perhaps its first assignment can be reading the ticket sleeve. I'd hate to discover we've promoted something that can't read.
after: Yes. 'Coming through' is why I'm standing over here with the tickets.

before: Does the helmet earn travel points? Its owner will want to exchange them for snacks.
after: Did he pack anything besides the helmet?

before: Only if it buys its own ticket. I am not explaining a separate seat for the headgear.
after: Oh, yes. A very small sandwich. He knows what takes priority.

before: Can your watch accept being wrong, or should I break the news to it privately?
after: How's your watch taking the news that it's wrong?

before: It's handling the news with dignity. No dramatic beeping. A very professional response.
after: Quietly. With dignity. I'm proud of it.

before: Less gracefully. I'm correcting the record. I'd like it noted that I did this before anyone made me.
after: I'm getting there. I've crossed my old times out, haven't I?

before: I'll check the new times with you. Tell the watch it hasn't lost its job. Please give its owner the same message.
after: You have. I'll check the new times with you. The watch can carry on being dignified.

before: I was going to say 'digital ghost'. A good theory, I thought. Very modern. No old-fashioned bedsheet.
after: I was going to say 'digital ghost.'

before: Going to? What's happened to it?
after: Was?

before: I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside until we know whether the machine made a mistake.
after: I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside.

before: Look at you. Keeping a perfectly good ghost out of the evidence until it's earned its place.
after: You see, now you've made it harder for me to tease you. I had a whole speech ready.

before: I'll find it a book while it waits. Something with a proper ending. It must be tired of unfinished business.
after: You could lend the ghost a book while it waits.

before: A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password. Getting it out of the library would be enough trouble.
after: A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password.

before: This panel looks like a very worried pear. I think it's realized we've brought notebooks.
after: That paint smear looks like a very worried pear. See the eyebrows?

before: Give it a place on the art wall, not the witness list. We have enough people to question without interviewing the paint.
after: I'd rather see who moved the panel. Before you give every splash a name.

before: Understood. Pear excluded from questioning. I'll tell it the good news when it stops looking so nervous.
after: Just the pear. It's called Pear.

before: Does the pear have an alibi? We shouldn't rule it out just because it's having a difficult day.
after: Easy to remember. Does Pear have an alibi?

before: The pear is paint, Dilo. Please don't make me put that in the notebook.
after: The pear is paint, Dilo.

before: Nobody move the pieces yet. I want to see which edges belong together before we make the message say something we like.
after: Leave them just there. We can still see the torn edges.

before: I was going to reach for it again. I'll suggest first. Better for the paper, slightly harder on my patience.
after: I only meant to catch it.

before: Good. Suggest away. Check the joins with me; if I try to force two edges together, you get to stop me.
after: I know. Come around here. I need someone to check the joins with me.

before: And keep the handwriting visible when we sleeve it. Edges first, words next. We'll want to read it without taking the whole thing apart again.
after: We'll put it in a sleeve when it fits. Keep the writing where we can see it.

before: That was a very particular look at the writing. Do you know whose it is?
after: Do you recognize it?

before: Maybe. The archive will have to back me up. I don't get to turn a memory into a fact just because I'm the oldest person at the table.
after: It feels familiar. I'd like to find another sample before I say more.

before: Then you've got the archive, we've got the joins, and Detective has the pieces. I like this plan. I can help without hurrying the paper.
after: I'll check this edge. You take the next one, Detective.

before: Three identical black instrument cases. Excellent. The objects have joined witness protection. We may have to give them new names.
after: I can tell the three cases apart now. That one was on the left.

before: Their names are on the labels. Whoever arranged the protection has made one fairly serious mistake.
after: Before you walked around the table, or after?

before: Weak cover identities. I could run this operation better with a marker pen and ten minutes.
after: Ah. I had a system until you asked that.

before: Please don't improve their labels. They've had a long rehearsal. Let's get them onto the right shelves before you start them on new careers.
after: I like the labels. They stay on the same case when I walk around it.

before: I'll check the shelves. I'm not explaining three freshly renamed instruments to their teacher.
after: Tell me before you change seats, Alio. I'm only just learning your system.

before: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally. I wasn't even playing. It just sat there showing me a score it knew I'd want to beat.
after: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally.

before: I've got the wristband file. Can you bear to leave your rival unsupervised while we find someone who can help with the record?
after: I've got the wristband file. Come on. I'll let you tell me how easily you could beat it on the way.

before: For the case. Tell it I haven't surrendered. And if the score changes while I'm away, I want a witness.
after: Easily. Walk slowly. I haven't told you about my best score yet.

before: I've paused my dramatic theory. It's waiting very patiently. Much better manners than people usually give it credit for.
after: I've paused my dramatic theory.

before: Yes. The muddy evidence requested a word. I'm trying this new thing where I listen before drawing a tunnel.
after: Yes. I want to get a proper look at the prints before I say anything else.

before: Then I'll be quiet too. We've got actual prints to compare, and I want to hear what you notice.
after: Then I'll be quiet too.

before: Both of you? I should photograph this. The family will never believe it happened without evidence.
after: Both of you? I should get a photograph. Nobody at home will believe me.

before: Footprints first. My good behavior can wait for the family album. Put it next to Mom finding her phone; I'd like this album to be fair.
after: Footprints first. Put my good behavior next to you finding your phone. I'd like the family album to be fair.

before: This parcel has met more helpful people than it can remember. If one more person says 'Leave it with me', we may need a map of its holidays.
after: Everyone who touched this parcel was helping. It must be exhausting to be that well looked after.

before: Then let's help it in a less creative order. Check the handoff before anybody moves it again.
after: Let's give it a rest. Nobody move it until we know where it belongs.

before: I'll guard it. Revolutionary idea: one label, one destination. No unauthorized helping while the Detective works.
after: I'll stay with it. Alio, if you're about to help, put your hands in your pockets.

before: What about morale biscuits? For the people. I haven't completely misunderstood the parcel.
after: I was going to get us some cookies. Difficult now.

before: Allowed. Bring enough for our Detective too. Advice for the parcel can wait until we've checked where it's meant to go.
after: Hands out, then. That's the first delivery here with a clear destination.

before:
I knew we kept those maps for a reason. Our table looks as if we've been collecting paper professionally.
We have. Every one is a solved case. I also kept mine because the stack looked impressive. Both things can be true.
after:
Fourteen selected maps. I knew we'd need all that careful filing.
I kept mine because the stack looked impressive. I've been showing people.

before:
They can. Let's lay out the selected maps before you start measuring your achievements with a ruler.
Useful evidence and an excellent stack. Let him have both.
after:
That explains why you asked if the librarian was coming round.
Let him show it off. He's usually showing me something he hasn't finished yet.

before: Then let me have some table. My elbow has become a paperweight. If there's anything else we must keep, you'll have to file me alongside it.
after: He can show them my elbow. It's been holding this corner down for ten minutes.

before: Empty rooms. We've been looking at everyone except nobody. I suppose nobody wasn't going to put a hand up.
after: We've been looking at where everyone stood. Now it's the rooms with nobody in them.

before: Nobody has been very quiet. Before we give it a medal, I should mention that it's contributed nothing to the conversation.
after: Nobody's been very patient. Hasn't interrupted once.

before: Already my favorite witness. No interruptions, no dramatic entrances, and no equipment requests.
after: Already my favorite witness.

before: Your brothers are right here, Luli. Besides, I've heard you explain a footnote over an entire dinner.
after: Luli, you once explained a footnote all the way through dinner. Your brothers barely managed to ask for the salt.

before: Which I enjoyed. But let's give nobody a turn. Detective, pull the maps closer; I want to see what we've been walking past.
after: I enjoyed that footnote. But I would like to hear what we've missed.

before: Clean hands. Flat map. No heroic folding. This plan is older than all your favorite excuses.
after: Clean hands, please. And no folding the old map to make room for your elbows.

before: Am I allowed one heroic finger? I only want to point. I can do it at a perfectly sensible distance.
after: May I point? I've got a very clean finger and nowhere else to put my excitement.

before: One clean finger, above a landmark. No prodding. The building has survived this long without you poking a new room into it.
after: Above the sleeve. Go on. I want to see what you've noticed.

before: We solved a whole parcel mystery, recovered your archive tools and earned permission for one finger. I was hoping for at least a whole hand.
after: All those cases, and he's finally been trusted with one finger.

before: A worthy investment. The sleeve can touch the map; your finger can hover. Now, who's going to help me line up the plans?
after: I trust the rest of him too. I just prefer it farther from my map.

before: I've put my tunnel proposal on a separate card. It looks much more convincing with a heading and a straight border.
after: I've put my tunnel theory on a separate card. With a proper heading. It looks quite convincing.

before: How much evidence is on the card? I'm asking before you draw a crest for it.
after: How much evidence is on the card?

before: At present? Decorative confidence. I gave that quite a lot of space.
after: At present? Decorative confidence.

before: I'd like a card. Some of my very organized plans are mostly that. I've been calling it 'being prepared' and hoping nobody asks for details.
after: I'd like a card. I've put that into several very organized plans.

before: Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience'. That's why I like your question, Luli. It used to annoy me terribly.
after: Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience.'

before: That's a lot of map. I'll clear some space. Nobody balance anything on the Detective's elbow; I've tried that system and can't recommend it.
after: That's a lot of map. Slide the folders over. Let's give our Detective some room.

before: Take your time. We're not going anywhere. If you need to stare at one corner for a while, I'll check the other one with you.
after: Take your time. I'll stay at this end so it doesn't curl up on you.

before: I can be quiet for one map. A big one. I'm making a serious offer here.
after: I can be quiet for one map. If that helps.

before: I've written that down. In pencil, to be fair.
after: It does. I'll save anything worth teasing you about until afterwards.

before: Make the call when you're ready. We're here.
after: There. All of us here, and space to think. Begin when you're ready.

before:
already proved.

HAPPY MAKERS COMMS
1 MIMI: No new clue. Use what you earned. Your Case Wall has the record; the panel's ready when you are.
2 DILO: Victory noise? I've been saving a very good one. I'm worried it's going to escape without permission.
